about > What is the information assistant / what are you?

used as a replacement for AI models like ChatGPT or Claude. Instead, the assistant should be used as a tool to answer any question
Freed Hardeman related.

to undergraduates, Faculty


David begins Psalm 27 with a question rooted in confidence: “The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?” (v. 1). David knew what it meant to face enemies, uncertainty, and danger. Yet he understood that the presence of trouble did not mean the absence of God. We often want God to remove everything that frightens us, but this psalm invites us to trust Him even while those things remain.

announceTest
Our courage grows as we remember who stands with us.

At the heart of the psalm, David reveals his deepest desire: to dwell in the Lord’s house and behold His beauty (v. 4). With so many urgent concerns surrounding him, David makes fellowship with God his greatest priority. That challenges us to examine what we seek most. We can become so consumed with asking God to change our circumstances that we neglect the invitation to draw closer to Him.

announceTest
Time spent in prayer, Scripture, and worship helps us see our circumstances through the assurance of His presence.

The psalm closes with an instruction many of us find difficult: “Wait on the LORD: be of good courage” (v. 14). Waiting requires faith because we cannot always see what God is doing or when an answer will come. Still, we can remain faithful in the responsibilities before us, pray honestly about our fears, and trust His goodness through the uncertainty.

records.heading: Chi Beta Chi (XBX, Chi Beta)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Chi Beta Chi (XBX, Chi Beta)
Chi Beta Chi is a social club that was established in 1989. Our mascot is the eagle, our letters are XBX, and our colors are purple and gold. Our mission statement is to provide opportunities for our members to become active socially, physically, mentally, and spiritually. Chi Beta has so many opportunities for our members to serve God and to serve others through mission trips to Wisconsin, the City of Children, and through various service projects around Henderson.

records.heading: Chi Beta Chi (XBX, Chi Beta)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Chi Beta Chi (XBX, Chi Beta)
We strive to be competitive in intramurals, Makin’ Music, Homecoming, and we seek to grow through retreats, meetings, and by being an encouragement to one another. The qualities we look for in our members are: Character, Leadership, Service, Tradition, and Royalty.

records.heading: Omega Chi (OK)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Omega Chi (OK)
Omega Chi is the newest club on campus. Established in 2022, we are confined by nothing but strive to excel in everything. Our motto is “For the pursuit of excellence.” This club was created by students who do not fit the mold of existing stereotypes. Here, you are free to be exactly who you are but challenged to become what The Lord has designed for you to be. We don’t look for skill, style, or status, but good people who love to have a good time and serve their good God in all they do.

records.heading: Omega Chi (OK)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Omega Chi (OK)
Our mascot is the panther. Like the panther, we are unique and exist in a diverse environment in which we thrive. Years from now, the members will continue to grow and succeed because of the foundation that the members of today establish. The Omega Chi panthers are here to stay.

records.heading: Phi Kappa Alpha (PKA, Phi Kappa)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Phi Kappa Alpha (PKA, Phi Kappa)
Established in 1938, Phi Kappa Alpha was created for men and women whose purpose was to exemplify and serve God in everything they do, to hold to the traditions of the past, and to strive to be a club of excellence on this campus. Phi Kappa Alpha will always compete to strive for the best in everything we do whether its Homecoming, Makin’ Music, or intramural athletics.

records.text:

records.heading: Sigma Rho (Sig)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Sigma Rho (Sig)
Sigma Rho is the oldest club on Freed-Hardeman’s campus and is founded on strong principles of family and tradition. We are characterized by our Greek letters, the Sigma standing for strength and the Rho for wisdom. We wear our black and gold colors with pride, the same way our Sigma Rho brothers and sisters wore them 101 years ago and the same way they will be worn 101 years from now. We bees have many mottos that are frequently used, but there is one that stands out among the rest.

records.heading: Sigma Rho (Sig)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Sigma Rho (Sig)
Our motto comes from a poem written by a club member many years ago. “It is the love I have for the things WE’VE done, that is why I am a Sigma Rho.” We don’t need a reminder that only the strong survive or anything like that because we don’t survive…we thrive. We thrive through the great memories we’ve made with one another. We thrive as we grow together in our spiritual walks with God. We thrive because we care about each other. We thrive because we are Sigma Rho.

records.heading: Xi Chi Delta (XC, Xi Chi, XCD)
records.text:
static information > external > fhu website > social clubs > Xi Chi Delta (XC, Xi Chi, XCD)
Xi Chi Delta was established in 2002 by a group of friends who wanted to make a difference on Freed-Hardeman’s campus. It remains as FHU’s only social club started by students for students. Our colors are navy and silver and our mascot is a Knight. The slogan of Xi Chi Delta is K.N.I.G.H.T.S., “Keeping Nothing Inside Glorifying Him Through Service.” Our foundation remains fixated on God, the single Being Who unites all of our hearts together in perfect unity.

records.heading: Xi Chi Delta (XC, Xi Chi, XCD)

records.heading: Freed-Hardeman University (FHU) Overview
records.text:
static information > gen overview fhu > Freed-Hardeman University (FHU) Overview
Freed–Hardeman University is a private university associated with the Churches of Christ and located in Henderson, Tennessee, United States. FHU is primarily undergraduate and residential. FHU also serves some commuting, part-time and adult students on-campus and through distance-learning programs.
FHU is governed by a board of trustees, all of whom are required to be members of Churches of Christ.

records.heading: Freed-Hardeman University (FHU) Overview

FHU courses are offered by 12 academic departments in 5 colleges: Arts and Sciences, Biblical Studies, Business, Education and Behavioral Sciences, and the Honors College.

records.heading: History of Freed-Hardeman University
records.text:
static information > gen overview fhu > History of Freed-Hardeman University
Freed–Hardeman traces its origin to the 1869 charter of a private high school and college for Henderson, the "Henderson Male Institute". FHU was known at various times as the "Henderson Masonic Male and Female Institute", "West Tennessee Christian College", or "Georgie Robertson Christian College". FHU was named Georgie Robertson Christian College after George Ann "Georgie" Robertson.

In the 1907 spring term Georgie Robertson Christian College closed. N. B.

records.text:
static information > gen overview fhu > History of Freed-Hardeman University
In the 1907 spring term Georgie Robertson Christian College closed. N. B. Hardeman, a Georgie Robertson Christian College alumnus, and A. G. Freed worked together to establish a new institution, the "National Teachers' Normal and Business College" to fill the educational void created in Henderson by the closing. The NTNBC was incorporated on May 21, 1907, but classes did not start until the fall of 1908. In 1919, it was renamed "Freed–Hardeman College" in honor of its founders.

records.heading: History of Freed-Hardeman University
records.text:
static information > gen overview fhu > History of Freed-Hardeman University
In 1919, it was renamed "Freed–Hardeman College" in honor of its founders. In February 1990, it became Freed–Hardeman University.

FHU did not accept African-American students until 1964. The first black graduate of FHU was Elizabeth Saunders in 1967.

FHU offers courses outside of the Henderson area in Memphis, Tennessee. FHU also offers European study abroad programs based at the FHU facility in Verviers, Belgium.

records.heading: History of Freed-Hardeman University
records.text:
static information > gen overview fhu > History of Freed-Hardeman University
Other study abroad opportunities at FHU include programs in Spain, Israel, Costa Rica, New York City, Canada, and Seoul.

FHU was granted an exception to Title IX in 2016 allowing discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation and gender identity where conflict exists with religious tenets.

During the 2019–2020 academic year, FHU university celebrated its 150th anniversary and a volume of university history, By the Grace of God: The Story of Freed–Hardeman University, was published.
